course_name_en: Development of Sustainable Machines and Systems
prerequisites: Basic engineering knowledge from Bachelor studies

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the essential features of industrial product development processes and the fundamental working and problem-solving methods for the successful development of products, especially with regard to sustainability and environmental compatibility.

Students can systematically plan and execute product developments independently of the industry. They know proven problem-solving methods and concrete methods for product optimization under the aspect of sustainability, they can evaluate the effect of these methods and select them appropriately. They can integrate essential computer-aided methods and procedures (CAE).
Students can evaluate the impact of different approaches to sustainable development of machines and systems against the background of the underlying requirements.
Students can independently develop more sustainable products based on the methods taught.

Students can implement current requirements for environmental compatibility, sustainability, and future-proof products in such a way that the 'footprint' of the developed products is significantly better than that of classically developed products.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the concept of sustainability
Overview of methods for sustainable development and design
Comparison of classic versus sustainable design using an example of a working machine
Comparison of classic versus sustainable design for a linked system
Exercise example: Development of a sustainable device
assessment_rules: A accompanying term paper will be prepared. The work can be done individually or in a small group, with the scope of work adjusted accordingly. The term paper involves analyzing an existing product, identifying levers to increase the sustainability index, and subsequent re-engineering to enhance sustainability. Documentation is done in written form (approx. 15-25 pages) and through a new product design using CAE. The product must consist of at least 2-3 functional assemblies.
